answer.generated: Concurrency control in a database management system primarily ensures that multiple transactions can execute simultaneously without causing data inconsistencies or errors. It achieves this by implementing mechanisms such as locks, which prevent conflicts when two transactions attempt to modify the same data concurrently. Locks are integral to concurrency control as they allow the system to manage access to shared resources efficiently. Additionally, view-equivalence plays a crucial role in ensuring that the illusion of serial execution is maintained, allowing users to perceive the database operations as if they were executed one after another, even though they may be interleaved. This relationship between concurrency control, locks, and view-equivalence is fundamental to maintaining data integrity and user satisfaction in concurrent database environments.
